device.name: Magic Display
device.notes:
Bluetooth-controlled LED displays for shoes, bags, hats, crafts. Uses Quintic (NXP QN-series) BLE chipset with QPP (Quintic Private Profile) on service 0xFEE9 (chipset is NOT family-wide Quintic: sibling Shining Glasses hardware is Panchip-based with a 0xFD00 OTA service, so Magic Display variants may likewise differ). All command traffic is AES-128-ECB encrypted via the native libAES.so (aes.keyExpansionDefault() is a JNI native method; the 16-byte key lives in the .so binary, NOT in Java — extract libAES.so to recover it). Commands are fixed 16-byte ASCII-named packets: [length, ASCII_CMD..., params..., zero_pad]. CORRECTION: there is NO connection-time 3-way handshake (the earlier claim was wrong). After connecting, the app simply queries the LED matrix type (STYPE) and parses the response. Bulk image transfer uses DATS (data_transfer_start) framing followed by data frames and DATCP (data_transfer_complete) — that is transfer framing, not an authentication handshake. Supports multiple display sizes: 5x36, 12x48, 14x56, 16x64 (reported via STYPE response). Monochrome 1-bit-per-pixel bitmap encoding (threshold: any RGB channel >= 128 = ON). Device identification by manufacturer-specific adv data: {0x54, 0x52, 0x00, 0x27} ("TR" + 0x0027). No pairing required. Shares the com.cdbwsoft BLE codebase with Shining Glasses. A secondary Texas Instruments profile (service 0xFFF0 / char 0xFFF1) is also supported for TI-based hardware variants. Also has OTA service at 0xFEE8 (Quintic OTA protocol). FEE9/9600 is the generic Quintic-SDK QPP profile reused by unrelated products (e.g. Zhiyun Crane V2 gimbal), so scanning by service UUID alone false-positives — the manufacturer-data prefix match is the real discriminator. CONFIDENCE: command/UUID mapping HIGH (jadx of com.tirohk.magicdisplay); AES key not present in the Java APK (native lib) — but two family keys are already public and are the first candidates to try on Magic Display hardware: 32672f7974ad43451d9c6c894a0e8764 (Shining Glasses/Mask) and 34522a5b7a6e492c08090a9d8d2a23f8 (iDeal LED).
Enrich-branch evidence: version 1.5.6 (versionCode 156) was inspected with jadx. Java class csh.tiro.cc.aes exposes cipher / invCipher / keyExpansion / keyExpansionDefault backed by lib/arm64-v8a/libAES.so; Agreement.getEncryptData() encrypts every command before write and Agreement.getDecodeData() decrypts notifications. Bulk pixel/image upload uses DATS on WRITE1, waits for DATSOK, sends data chunks on WRITE2, then sends DATCP and waits for DATCPOK. CORRECTION (2026-07-31 verification): three independent sibling implementations (Staars gist, timhodson/ble-led-badge protocol.py, Jhan-vasquez-dev/shining-glasses PROTOCOL.md) all send bulk image data on WRITE2 (960a) UNENCRYPTED in ~100-byte [len][seq][payload] chunks (~98-byte payloads) — not AES-encrypted 16-byte chunks — with per-packet flow control (the device returns an encrypted REOK notification after each bulk packet and the sender must wait). Caveat: sibling-app evidence, not the magicdisplay APK itself; re-check whether Agreement.getEncryptData() is applied to WRITE2 writes in com.tirohk.magicdisplay. WRITE3 (960b) carries live DIY single-pixel writes (unencrypted 20-byte packets 05 RR GG BB II 00..., sibling evidence). Multi-frame animation uses a MANY <count> <profile> transaction with per-frame DATS/data/DATCP, closed by MANCPOK (sibling DiyMutiAgreement). Agreement.parseType maps STYPE5X36, STYPE12X48, STYPE14X56, STYPE16X64 and N-suffixed variants. Additional observed app features include LIGHTON/LIGHTOFF torch control, MODE 7 music/rhythm mode backed by libint16fft.so, SMVEW DIY sync draw, LEDFIRST/LEDSECOND chained display selection, CALL notification passthrough, SCHD/STSC scheduling, and ANIM animation selection.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Identify by service UUID and the manufacturer-data prefix rather than by name, since these units advertise without a stable local name.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

data_transfer_start.description: Start bulk data transfer. hi/lo = big-endian 16-bit data length.

multi_frame_animation_start.description: Multi-frame animation transaction: MANY <count> <profile>, then per-frame DATS/data/DATCP; the device closes with MANCPOK (sibling evidence: shining-glasses DiyMutiAgreement). Exact byte layout TBD.

query_device_type.description: Query display dimensions. Response on notify: 'STYPE5X36', 'STYPE12X48', 'STYPE16X64', etc.

characteristics.name: Command (WRITE1)
characteristics.notes: AES-128-ECB, fixed static key. static_key OMITTED: the key is in the native libAES.so (loaded via aes.keyExpansionDefault, a JNI method) and is not present in the decompiled Java APK. Recover it by extracting the 16-byte key from libAES.so — or first try the two public family keys: 32672f7974ad43451d9c6c894a0e8764 (Shining Glasses/Mask) and 34522a5b7a6e492c08090a9d8d2a23f8 (iDeal LED); shared cdbwsoft codebase, unproven for this app. Confidence: HIGH structure. Evidence: com/tirohk/magicdisplay/MainApplication.java:26 (keyExpansionDefault); csh/tiro/cc/aes.java:11 (native); com/cdbwsoft/library/ble/BleManager.java:50-57.

characteristics.name: Bulk Data (WRITE2)
characteristics.notes: Bulk image data channel. CORRECTION: per three independent sibling-app implementations (Staars gist, timhodson/ble-led-badge protocol.py, Jhan-vasquez-dev/shining-glasses PROTOCOL.md) bulk data here is UNENCRYPTED ~100-byte [len][seq][payload] chunks (~98-byte payloads), not AES-128-ECB 16-byte chunks; the device acks each packet with an encrypted REOK notification on the notify char (per-packet flow control). Caveat: sibling-app evidence — re-check against the actual com.tirohk.magicdisplay APK before relying on this.

characteristics.name: Auxiliary (WRITE3)
characteristics.notes: Live DIY pixel writes: unencrypted 20-byte packets 05 RR GG BB II 00... (sibling evidence: shining-glasses PROTOCOL.md).

characteristics.name: TI Command
characteristics.notes: TI-variant command characteristic; same AES-128-ECB native key (key OMITTED, in libAES.so). Evidence: BleManager.java:52,58.
